जङ्गम, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. गम्),
moving, movable, locomotive, that which has motion
as opposed to that which is stationary, living; a
living being (= जगत् in the earlier language); de-
rived from living beings; [cf. Goth. gagga; Germ.
Gang.]
—जङ्गम-कुटी, f. a parasol, a chattar or
umbrella (‘movable house’).
—जङ्गम-त्व, अम्,
n. the state of having motion, movableness.
जङ्गम जङ्गम. See p. 335, col. 3.

जङ्क्ष् जङ्क्ष्, cl. 1. P. जङ्क्षति, a various
reading for क्षज् or क्षञ्ज्.
जङ्ग जङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of a man.

जङ्गपूग जङ्गपूग, अस्, m. wickedness,
sin (?).

जङ्गल जङ्गल, अस्, आ, अम्, arid, sterile,
desert; (अस्), m. a desert, waste or overgrown land,
any arid or sterile region, any wild or uninhabited
country, a jungle; (अस्, अम्), m. n. flesh, meat; [cf.
जाङ्गल and जङ्गुल.]

जङ्गाल, अस्, m. a land-mark, a limit, a boundary,
a ridge of earth running along the edge of a field for
collecting water and forming a passage over it, a balk.

जाङ्गल जाङ्गल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जङ्गल),
arid; sparingly grown with trees &c. but nevertheless
fertile; rural, picturesque, diversified with hill, vale,
wood, and water; found or existing in such a district;
desert, covered with jungle; wild, not tame (as an
animal &c.); savage, barbarous; (अस्), m. the franco-
line partridge; N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a
people; (ई), f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus; (अम्), n.
flesh; game, the flesh of deer &c.
जङ्गुल, अम्, n. poison, venom.

जाङ्गुल, अम्, n. poison, venom, = जङ्गुल; the
fruit of the Jālinī, a kind of cucumber; (ई), f.
knowledge of poisons, the possession of charms or
drugs and employment of them as antidotes; a pot-
herb, Luffa Acutangula; an epithet of Durgā.

जङ्गिड जङ्गिड, अस्, m., N. of a plant
which is worn as an amulet.

जङ्घ जङ्घ, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. जन्,
or corrupted from जङ्गा fr. rt. गा, to go, or fr. rt.
जंह्; cf. जघन), N. of a Rakṣas; (आ), f. the
shank or lower part of the leg from the ankle to the
knee; (in the earlier language also) the upper part
of the leg; a part of a bedstead; [cf. Old Germ.
scinkel; Germ. Schenkel.]
—जङ्घा-कर, अस्, ई,
अम्, or जङ्घा-करिक, अस्, आ, अम्, active with the
legs, running quickly, a runner.
—जङ्घा-कारिक,
अस्, m. a runner, a courier, an express.
—जङ्घा-
त्राण, अम्, n. armour or protection for the legs,
cuisses or greaves.
—जङ्घा-बन्धु, उस्, m., N. of
a man.
—जङ्घा-रथ, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्),
m. pl. his descendants.
—जङ्घारि (˚घा-अरि), इस्,
m., N. of a man.

जङ्घाल, अस्, आ, अम्, running swiftly, quick, rapid,
going quickly; (अस्), m. a courier; a deer, an antelope.
जङ्घिका, f. a diminutive fr. जङ्घा.

जाङ्घिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जङ्घा), swift of foot,
a courier; relating to or belonging to the leg; (अस्),
m. a courier, a running footman, an express; a
camel; a kind of antelope; [cf. कपि-जाङ्घिका.]
जङ्घिल, अस्, आ, अम्, running swiftly, quick, rapid.
जाङ्गलि, इस्, m. a snake-catcher; [cf. जाङ्गुलि.]
जाङ्गलिक, अस्, m. a snake-charmer, = जङ्गुलिक.

जाङ्गुलि, इस्, m. a snake-catcher, a dealer in anti-
dotes, a conjuror.

जाङ्गुलिक, अस्, m. a snake-catcher, a snake-doctor,
one who pretends by charms to cure the bite of snakes
or other venomous animals, a dealer in antidotes &c.

जाङ्घनी जाङ्घनी, f. (fr. जङ्घा), the thigh;
(perhaps a wrong form for जाघनी.)

जाङ्घाप्रहतिक or जाङ्घाप्रहृतिक, अस्, ई,
अम् (fr. जङ्घा-प्रहत or -प्रहृत), produced
by a blow with the leg.
जाङ्घालायन, अस्, m. (fr. जङ्घाल), N. of a man.

जाङ्घि, a patronymic from Jaṅgha or metronymic
from Jaṅghā.

जङ्घन्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens.),
being repeatedly struck, being greatly wounded.
